key_insight: K/Rb-based lead-free double perovskites beta2SnGeX6 are predicted by DFT to be thermodynamically stable, mechanically ductile, and highly tunable from wide-gap photovoltaic absorbers to narrow-gap thermoelectric/optoelectronic materials by changing the halogen.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a lead-free, cubic perovskite platform with composition-controlled bandgaps and low lattice thermal conductivity, making them promising for solar cells, tandem devices, photodetectors, and waste-heat recovery.
method: Density functional theory screening of six compositions: K/Rb with Cl, Br, I
Computed formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor for stability assessment
Analyzed elastic, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties from first-principles calculations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 eV to 0.64 eV and a peak thermoelectric figure of merit of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The results are theoretical predictions; real device performance may differ due to synthesis defects, phase purity, carrier doping, and temperature-dependent stability.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
